items.title: Why canonical a.e. representatives do not automatically carry classical scores

source.edition: arXiv:2010.03106v4, as cited by SPHMC arXiv:2609.06906v1
source.attribution: Lee--Shen--Tian differentiate an explicit smooth ratio; SPHMC cites that contraction. ASTIS records the separate formal representative-safety prerequisite; no author endorsement implied.

items.statement: For the restricted-Gaussian fibers, the explicit pointwise normalized log-density ratio has affine score (y-y')/eta. A faithful canonical-Fisher formalization must keep that smooth representative explicit: arbitrary almost-everywhere equality does not by itself transport classical gradients.
assumptions: The counterexample is over the Dirac probability measure at zero.

obligations.label: Preserve the explicit smooth score representative rather than transporting classical gradients through arbitrary a.e. equality

bindings.boundary: Rules out one unsound canonical-score adapter only; no SPHMC analytic conclusion is promoted.

assumption_deltas.source: Lee--Shen--Tian differentiate an explicit pointwise smooth normalized log-density ratio and obtain (y-y')/eta.
assumption_deltas.lean: Mathlib's llr is a specific Radon--Nikodym-based function, but its available identification with the explicit smooth ratio is only almost everywhere; the bound theorem rules out using that fact alone to transport classical gradients.
assumption_deltas.reason: Classical derivatives depend on local pointwise behavior, not only on a measure-theoretic equivalence class.
